public_rationale: Google reported strong launch scores on image and video reasoning tests. Those results weigh against a blanket description of poor visual reasoning, but do not establish reliable physical reasoning. The evidence reviewed does not adequately measure the frequency or breadth of the failures Marcus describes. Neither selected mistakes nor benchmark leadership settles the combined claim.
limitations: The usable outcome evidence is company-reported.
The claim's qualitative threshold remains ambiguous.
Later evaluations cannot automatically be assigned to the launch-period model.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Gemini 3's visual and physical reasoning remain poor.

statement.excerpt: Visual and physical reasoning are still a mess.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that Gemini 3 remains substantially unreliable at visual and physical reasoning, despite its benchmark leadership.
The subject is the launch version of Gemini 3 Pro. The target period is its November 18 announcement through the November 19 post.
A few selected mistakes would establish fallibility, but would not alone establish generally poor performance. Leadership over other models would not alone establish dependable performance.
criteria.support_condition: Representative, reproducible evaluations of the launch model show frequent substantive failures in both visual and physical reasoning, particularly on tasks people ordinarily solve reliably.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations show consistently dependable performance in both areas, including unfamiliar tasks and appropriate human comparisons.
